lessons.title: Examples and datasets
lessons.subtitle: Week 2: Learning from data
lessons.body:
A dataset is a collection of examples. Examples may contain text, numbers, images, or labels. More examples do not automatically mean better-quality data.

Offline practice: Create six fictional examples of library visits with weekday and visitor count. Write your reasoning before looking at the quiz answers. Record one limitation or uncertainty. You can use paper or local notes; an online AI tool is optional.

Recap: explain yesterday’s key idea from memory, then check your notes. After a break, start with this recap and the first small step of today’s activity.

Complete all three quiz questions before moving on.
takeaways: A dataset is a collection of examples. Examples may contain text, numbers, images, or labels. More examples do not automatically mean better-quality data.
Apply the idea through the offline activity.
Keep reasoning, evidence, and limitations with your artifact.

lessons.title: Features and labels
lessons.subtitle: Week 2: Learning from data
lessons.body:
Features are inputs used by a model. In supervised learning, a label is the target outcome provided for training. Choose features available when the prediction must be made.

Offline practice: For predicting a fictional bus delay, separate available inputs from the delay label. Write your reasoning before looking at the quiz answers. Record one limitation or uncertainty. You can use paper or local notes; an online AI tool is optional.

Recap: explain yesterday’s key idea from memory, then check your notes. After a break, start with this recap and the first small step of today’s activity.

Complete all three quiz questions before moving on.
takeaways: Features are inputs used by a model. In supervised learning, a label is the target outcome provided for training. Choose features available when the prediction must be made.
Apply the idea through the offline activity.
Keep reasoning, evidence, and limitations with your artifact.

lessons.title: Supervised learning
lessons.subtitle: Week 2: Learning from data
lessons.body:
Supervised learning uses examples paired with target outcomes. A message classifier can learn from messages labelled spam or not spam. Incorrect labels can mislead training.

Offline practice: Label six invented messages and explain why an ambiguous message needs review. Write your reasoning before looking at the quiz answers. Record one limitation or uncertainty. You can use paper or local notes; an online AI tool is optional.

Recap: explain yesterday’s key idea from memory, then check your notes. After a break, start with this recap and the first small step of today’s activity.

Complete all three quiz questions before moving on.
takeaways: Supervised learning uses examples paired with target outcomes. A message classifier can learn from messages labelled spam or not spam. Incorrect labels can mislead training.
Apply the idea through the offline activity.
Keep reasoning, evidence, and limitations with your artifact.

lessons.title: Unsupervised learning
lessons.subtitle: Week 2: Learning from data
lessons.body:
Unsupervised learning looks for structure without supplied target labels. Groups of similar examples do not automatically have meaningful names or causal explanations.

Offline practice: Group six fictional books by similarity and describe how a different grouping rule changes the result. Write your reasoning before looking at the quiz answers. Record one limitation or uncertainty. You can use paper or local notes; an online AI tool is optional.

Recap: explain yesterday’s key idea from memory, then check your notes. After a break, start with this recap and the first small step of today’s activity.

Complete all three quiz questions before moving on.
takeaways: Unsupervised learning looks for structure without supplied target labels. Groups of similar examples do not automatically have meaningful names or causal explanations.
Apply the idea through the offline activity.
Keep reasoning, evidence, and limitations with your artifact.

lessons.title: Reinforcement learning
lessons.subtitle: Week 2: Learning from data
lessons.body:
Reinforcement learning involves actions, feedback, and a reward objective. A reward is a design choice; maximising it may produce behaviour the designer did not intend.

Offline practice: Design a fictional study-game reward and identify one way someone could earn it without learning. Write your reasoning before looking at the quiz answers. Record one limitation or uncertainty. You can use paper or local notes; an online AI tool is optional.

Recap: explain yesterday’s key idea from memory, then check your notes. After a break, start with this recap and the first small step of today’s activity.

Complete all three quiz questions before moving on.

Weekly completion task: save this week’s practice artifact. Confirm four steps: explain a key idea (recap); complete the practice activity (practice); record what you would verify and where (plan); show your artifact and explain one improvement (demonstrate).
takeaways: Reinforcement learning involves actions, feedback, and a reward objective. A reward is a design choice; maximising it may produce behaviour the designer did not intend.
Apply the idea through the offline activity.
Keep reasoning, evidence, and limitations with your artifact.
